AI reliability / October 2026

Build the checks around the model

What my outbound pipeline taught me about putting operational rules in code.

My outbound pipeline uses three LLM agents for enrichment, routing, and drafting. Those are useful places for contextual reasoning. The operating rules around them need a different treatment.

A do-not-contact record needs to stop the workflow. A reply needs to stop follow-up. An unverified email needs to be checked before sending. These rules should be explicit in the system that runs the work.

In the pipeline, do-not-contact checks run at three stages, verification happens before send, and a cross-channel reply-stop prevents continued follow-up. There is also a human approval gate before a message ships.

The distinction shapes how I think about applied AI: use the model where interpretation helps, and make the boundaries around its output inspectable. A well-written prompt is one part of that design.

The result I can point to today is throughput: personalized outreach grew from about ten to more than sixty messages a day. To tell the full business story, response quality and downstream outcomes need their own measurement.
